一代看似有很多流派，但其实每把进钢铁商店永远是在找多重，进魔法商店永远在找返回，薪火升级永远都选过牌，要不是中间有个神殿，那每把都是一个模子刻出来的。 但是二代不一样了，现在单位升级百花齐放，二元性、小石头，每把都是不一样的组合，再也不是那个只有一种升级的商店了。魔法商店可以购买去消耗简直是天才设计，很多卡乍看没用，但是一旦搭配上去消耗就脱胎换骨，甚至一代那些消耗神卡也可以去消耗。 部署阶段的加入也是神之设计，让一代中不存在的多核阵容焕发新生，再也不是选定一个单位打到底了。 既然可以上多个单位，薪火的房间格子升级也得到了史诗级加强，事实上现在薪火升级也不再是抽牌一家独大了，三种升级各有利弊，双格子升级也能经常出现，甚至有七核全部站满的局，就连双费用升级都不是无稽之谈。 成长方式也不同于一代的简单粗暴，变得隐晦而巧妙起来，我甚至在没有任何成长法术的近乎绝望的对局中，搞出六个500攻肥猪和一个1000攻多重站在同一层，成功拿下比赛，简直就像变魔术，这是在一代里无法想象的。 敌人强度也相应提升。有些敌人机制乍看很阴间，但其实是给我方新机制的发挥创造了完美的条件，并不是一拍脑袋乱设计的。 总之制作组还真是开窍了，一代有多烂，二代就有多好

非常好的肉鸽+自走棋形式的游戏，继承了一代的优秀设计，同时在美术和机制上做出了非常多的拓展，可以说是延续了制作组的独特风格。 个人主观认为，游戏最黄金的时间只有10-20小时，这段时间对游戏的机制有足够的新鲜感，同时10个种族自由搭配，十几个篝火自由选择，大量的个性化挑战，量大管饱每一局都是全新体验。 但是在过了这段时间之后，由于敌人种类较少，契约等级的提升主要通过数值压制来体现，此时就会体验到游戏中非常欠考虑的因素。 首先是解锁要素，每个职业在5级解锁副英雄，10级才能解锁一个职业的所有卡牌和遗物，这就导致了整个解锁区间非常漫长，你需要反复打同一个职业并且至少达到中盘才能解锁全部卡牌。如果想要解锁全部职业的全卡牌，保守估计需要50小时以上。 其次就是数值和游戏内核问题，游戏低契约和高契约说是两个职业都不为过，高契约的后期boss血量是0契约的3倍，各种特效也是增强版，因此高契约对整个build组件要求非常高，但是游戏中获取卡牌的途径非常少，正常情况下只有战斗结束和事件以及路线中可以选择卡牌，因此build构建非常看脸。同时，商人的词条由于也是随机刷新，更是加剧了这一点，运气占了极大的比重。 然后是游戏资料预览问题，游戏内的卡牌预览功能形同虚设，因为只有当你解锁并遇见过这个卡牌或是怪物，你才能在预览中查看他们，而你玩的较少的职业，预览里基本就是一片空白。 以上三点单拎出来都是小问题，但是组合在一起就变成了重磅组合拳。你想在高进阶玩新职业，但是你连这个职业有什么卡牌什么机制都看不到，很多强力的卡牌核心甚至都需要高等级才能解锁，在战斗中也不知道这个职业卡牌间有什么联动，为了通关只能极端保守的抓牌，而由于前面提到的运气因素极大，你保守抓牌就意味着你放弃了一半的上限，除非玩某些单职业带狗都能通关的强力职业，不然体验极差。 所以为了升级，只能用新职业反复打低进阶，但低进阶难度过低，导致实际上就是毫无乐趣的重复劳作。游戏内的挑战关卡看似种类繁多，实际上后期大量关卡都是纯粹恶意，这点看解锁率就能佐证，需要反复的roll开局才能通关。因此，可以说，一旦了解了部分游戏机制想要深入游玩，就必然会被这个游戏大量的硬烧时间的欠缺打磨的内容恶心。 如果非要做类比，这游戏就像是一盘烧的色红油重红烧肉，初一口满嘴留香，但是第二口再吃下去，只会觉得油腻不堪。再参考这个价格，个人建议打折再考虑购入。

3费弃牌抽5，设计师到底有没有动过脑子？纯粹是对无限流哈气哈魔怔了。觉者道钉也被直接砍废，是不是默认玩家拿到这两张牌就有去消耗和减2费的石头还能再复制一张啊？除了这俩最有代表性的其他诸如祭品石碑等强力过牌组件也都被砍。本身过牌机制就残疾还搁那惦记你那b下回合加抽？那么鼓励一层开战还要拖慢玩家启动搞这种左右脑互搏的设计？我真不理解一个PVE游戏为什么还要砍原本可以让玩家爽的流派，哪怕你加强敌人都比盲目削弱来的明智。

玩某游戏某续作吃了一嘴屎有感，火车2是标杆性的续作超越原作的。本次平衡改动证明制作组绝大部分卡（特别是一代卡）都能改到点子上。 一代玩了1000+h，双随五百连胜。二代可以说完美替代了一代。二代只有两个氏族的demo我都玩了70h，那时我就认为设计理念上最大的进步就是从一代的养唯一大哥到二代的可以堆人，实现这点的改动是新增了部署阶段抽上所有战旗单位，弱战旗不再会使大哥上手变晚。这样变相使所有单位不分强弱都有上场/过渡机会了。所以我认为一代的融合机制不回来比较好，二代这帮高质量单位再融合不知道能创造出什么三体人。 我玩过的这么多出续作的游戏中，某游戏制作组说要适合新人玩，结果难度拉满没有正反馈。暗黑地牢2从前作的rpg变成了肉鸽，又因为平衡性不好，平衡补丁一团乱麻，差评颇多。hades2没有改动游戏类型，但是因为试玩版发售太早和平衡性不佳有一些差评。文明7不用说了，大改了时代机制给玩家喂屎，烂完了。异星工厂（我最喜欢的游戏没有之一）出的dlc没有横向扩展游戏内容，而是纵向整了花活还把老版的蓝图改不兼容了，我至今都没玩下去。模拟农场25一点新东西都没，画面也没什么提升，卖的贵而且失去了上一代优秀Mod的支持，刚发售多半差评突然就被控评到好评如潮了，我亲眼见证。CS2除了画面改进了，游戏流畅度和合理性变差了。OW2喜提steam7%好评率。以上游戏我均是大几百或几千小时。 综上所列，游戏想把续作出好实属不易，又不能没有创新，又不能革命太过头，又不能缺乏试玩和及时准确的修改补丁，又要兼容前代玩家。火车2是我玩过的游戏中续作出的最合格的。同时，期待爬塔2。塔2打磨了很久了，反倒车2看起来像是为了赶在塔2之前发售赶工出来的。2月还只有两个氏族的demo，5月就发出来了。上线时候底子打的好但是平衡性有不少缺点，至今能陆陆续续修复一些，就证明了火车2设计的合格。 3/24更新： 1、塔2我已经骂过了，制作组自己作死，且游戏理解水平太低且职业态度太差，真得学学车2制作组不刁难玩家，制作速度也非常快量大管饱。我还以为会延续卡牌游戏出二代不容易翻车的特点，塔2自己飘了 2、砍无限是对的，砍了无限同时加了数值，不像塔2楞头砍无限砍运转砍加费，弱的也不补偿
突然更新，真的死吗了，改了之后把我的轮椅改没了，要我这个残疾人怎么玩，三费的阿尔法是人啊，本来启动就慢，他活了砍了三点攻击力更是无语，对于没有移动需求的萨拉路来说约等于就是风险操作的下位替代，结果还砍，死妈了

先声明一下，怪物火车2是我玩过的最好玩的单机游戏，我一共打了385小时，拿了166个契约10泰坦皇冠。我打差评的唯一原因就是这游戏的风险提示做得完全不到位，我打契约10泰坦皇冠攒到25连胜以后，第26局（也是影祖的最后一个皇冠）也轻松打到了天使，结果就因为一时兴起去群里传了一下神器截图，导致忘记了开泰坦精华就点了开始战斗，之前打的所有连胜就这么直接断了。这实在是太过挫败了，我直接选择了弃游。虽然我承认一部分原因是我自己的疏忽，但我是真的不理解，在泰坦精华选项这么容易出问题的关键环节，不应该设置个提示弹窗吗？玩家没开泰坦精华，直接像放弃游戏那样生成一个弹窗提醒：“您确定要这样做吗？这将会终结您当前的xx连胜”，这样就完全能避免此类恶性事故。如果你问我为什么不设置默认开启精华的选项，那我要告诉你，因为开挑战和开精华是同一个操作，是会互相影响的，我80%的挑战都会开启，如果在飞行BOSS这里直接不选，是非常反直觉的，一样容易因为下意识点一下而出事。我是真心希望官方能看到我的测评，并改善这个问题。

Wow what a let down. Loved the first game, played the hell out of it and kept playing the daily challenges long after I was done with the base game. Played this a bunch, and not having as much fun with it. I am absolutely baffled that people think this game is better than the first. The first game had much better balance, and the rng of the draft choices as well as the "shop" options was much more fair. The boss design in this game is particularly poor. Stryx and Hallow are a ridiculously punishing pairing that requires dedicated builds to beat. How am I supposed to have fun with a game with so many options when only a few of the options can actually succeed. What is the fun of that? I am a veteran gamer with hours of play in all types of strategy games. I have tried a particular dimensional portal challenge over 100 times and have never been successful. This type of game design is not fun to play, and consumers should shun poor design. This is a strategy game, not a souls like hack and slash where my inputs can help balance the difficulty of the game. There have been multiple times I have been unable to complete even the second battle due to poor card choices and not enough ability to do damage. In later battles it becomes ridiculously difficult. There are enemies with 200-350 health and my troops can only do 25-40 in damage with upgrades. If the right upgrades aren't available (largestone, multistrike, etc) then you cannot level your troops enough to even scratch the enemies. How is this fun? How is this good game design? Don't tell me to rely on spells. How can I kill 300 health enemies with spells that do 10 damage? WTF is this? Why are the first few battles so damn easy but the later battles are so difficult? Where is a normal power curve? I'm sorry but I've lost faith in the reviewing community for having this as "Overwhelmingly Positive". Please just play the first one instead, it is actually fun and balanced. Avoid this convoluted mess of a game. They tried to do too much and ruined a good formula.

The game itself is fine... but... that's it? There is so little content it's actually baffling. Ooops, 62 hours in and I haven't left a positive review, how rude of me. This is shaping up to be one of my most-played card games of all time, and that has to do with two important things that are in conflict with each other: balance and variety. Theoretically, you want a card game with lots of different strategies, abilities, power ups, all of that, otherwise it gets stale. The thing is, the more variety there is, the harder it is to find a sense of balance and fair challenge. This game is not easy, not at all (in fact, the true final boss fight felt like it required a broken build to even be possible) but at the base level of difficulty, it feels as it should, "tough but fair". The really impressive thing, though, is that in the context of that "tough but fair" balance, we find not only a bunch of new ways to play, but eventually, you can have all of the decks/styles from the last game (Monster Train 1 is incredible, I recommend you play that first, it's worth it) too, AND mix and match them with the new decks! So it's 5 new ways to play and all the permutations therein, plus, the old 6 ways and the new permutations. I'm not a math guy but I think that's an absurd amount of player choice if you break it down. I will say, I prefer the OG clans. This game has some really great clans, but especially when it comes to some of the new heroes, they just don't feel that worthwhile to choose. I really felt like I was unlocking truly great styles after the first couple, though, so it's worth it to work through the early game... and eventually I did learn some of the missed opportunities available with the clans I don't like but... I mean... mushroom guys versus almost any other option? Mushroom is clearly best. That kind of thing. Regardless, the game blows the first one out of the water in terms of options, especially with the new equipment system, and it's got an amazing set of challenges... at first I avoided them because I was like "I don't want the game to be HARDER"... but aside from some stinkers, I'm actually super impressed by how these challenges seem to be explicitly designed to make the early game harder in specific ways but then lead to totally cracked builds. You can actually have more of a power fantasy with many of the "challenges" than you can in the base game if you figure out the puzzle of how to not lose due to the new constraints and that's just 10/10 game design, chef's kiss, WOW. I struggle to think of major complaints. This is certainly worth the price of anyone who likes games like this. I'd like it to be maybe 10% easier but it is what it is, and clearly, I'm in the minority given how many levels of extra difficulty you can add. It just has that slay the spire problem where you can absolutely crush an entire run, like literally zero damage/perfect, and then the final boss just eats you for breakfast and sends you packing with a loss, which I really dislike... but most of these games share this issue and at least in this one you can clearly predict what is coming and try to prepare for it once you understand some of the specific final problems to deal with. Overall. I mean, 62 hours, right? Like I usually am done with games like this in less than 30. That's all you need to know. I will say, though, if you haven't played the first one, go buy that first. It's a truly incredible game, too, and you'll learn the old decks in their native environment and then enjoy taking them for a spin eventually here. I see people in reviews saying it's just straight-up better than the old game so why bother but I disagree... the old game is great!

Monster Train 2 is by far the best roguelike I have ever played. Everything that makes MT1 so good got brought forward with more than twice the amount of content, extra modes, plenty of challenges, new card types, and more. I have barely scratched the surface of playing every faction combination because my god there are SO many and all of them are fun. The new factions of Underlegion and Banish are incredibly fun to play and have such unique mechanics that only exist because of how Monster Train works. It is punishing and difficult while also being really fun and easy to break the game, however all the "break the game" strategies have counterplay in the game that need you to devise counter play to them. Needing answers to a whole lot of problems makes the game super fun. Questions like, "What is my Seraph answer?" "How do I protect my backliners" and "How do I turn scaling into winning" is so fun. It is a scaling roguelike where the answer isn't to just scale harder, the answer is to figure out how your scaling actually hits the enemy units effectively. The Titans are the most interesting True Final Boss out of any roguelike I have played, and more fun the Last Divinity. On my roguelike tierlist, this game got its own tier above S, it is THAT good.
It has a lot of replayability, even after every clan is maxed out.

this game is an interesting concept and has the potential for a lot of fun, but the high end covenant levels are just lazy game design. if you have built a card game, one with soul and personality, one that makes you want to play more and more cards and make the best little deck you can, as this team has, then i do not understand why the method for making the game "more difficult" is to let you play it less. rather than design interesting interactions, they have opted to flood your deck with cards that not only waste your draws but also actively punish you if you dont play them. it doesnt really matter what cards are in your deck if you just draw 5 of these blight cards (you start with 2 every run and will certainly acquire more in battles) the only way to reliably circumvent this is to, of course, buy the dlc faction that lets you eliminate these cards from your deck (a feat no other faction is capable of on a consistent basis). they have invented a problem and sold you a solution instead of fixing their mistake. this is extremely disappointing. the game shifts very rapidly from "yes and" to "straight up don't" and that is a damn shame.

Monster Train 2 is the best deckbuilder I've played to date (and I've played a lot). The game has all the right pieces, nice art, banger of a soundtrack, and exciting yet strategic gameplay. For me, the game has a great balance despite a lot of RNG being involved. A good player will beat the Titans at Cov 10 most of the time but a majority of those runs would be lost if the player didn't think ahead strategically in the early and mid game. While there is an occasional run where you are simply given all the right pieces and, thus, is a breeze, most runs reach a point where the player has to consider their over all strategy and plan for winning. The soundtrack and sound design by Jordan Chin is so good and may be even better than its predecessor. The only weak spot is the story and the dialogue scenes. It just doesn't do much for me but I'm okay with that for this genre. 5/5 Stars.
